'''''Wigandia urens''''', [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonyms]] including '''''Wigandia caracasana''''', known as '''fiberglass plant''' and the '''Caracus wigandia''', is a plant in the family [[Namaceae]].

== Description==
It is an erect shrubby plant up to 6 meters tall that can develop [[trichome]]s and urticating hairs with [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]] 2.5 to 10 cm long and oval leaves 5.5 to 50 cm long and 3.5 to 37 cm wide. The flowers develop calyx lobes 4 to 15 mm long, with broadly campanulate [[Perianth|corollas]] whose colors can differ between purple, blue or whitish lilac 1.5 to 2.2 cm long. It has stamens attached to the corollas for a quarter of their length and hairy filaments 1.2 to 1.5 cm long in the lower 3 quarters. It has slightly oblong anthers 3 to 6 mm.<ref name="flora">{{cite book |last1=Calderón de Rzedowski |first1=Graciela |last2=Rzedowski |first2=Jerzy |year=2001 |orig-year=1979 |title=Flora fanerogámica del Valle de México |trans-title=Phanerogamic flora of the Valley of Mexico |language=Spanish |edition=2 |publication-place=Xalapa, Mexico |publisher=Instituto de Ecología A.C. |pages=601–602 |isbn=978-607-7607-36-6 }}</ref><ref name="nash">{{cite book |last1=Nash |first1= Dorothy L. |date=1979-04-14 |editor-last1=Gómez Pompa |editor-first1=Arturo |title=Hydrophyllaceae |url=https://libros.inecol.mx/index.php/FV/catalog/view/483/546/2548 |series=Flora de Veracruz |language=Spanish |volume=5 |publication-place=Xalapa, Mexico |publisher=Instituto Nacional de Investigaciones sobre Recursos Bióticos |pages=31–37 |isbn=84-89600-09-0 |access-date=2025-08-26 }}</ref><ref name="conabio">{{cite web |last1=Hanan Alipi |first1=Ana María |last2=Mondragón Pichardo |first2=Juana |date=2009-07-23 |title=Ortiga de tierra caliente |url=http://www.conabio.gob.mx/malezasdemexico/hydrophyllaceae/wigandia-urens/fichas/ficha.htm |trans-title=Fiberglass plant |language=Spanish |publisher=[[Comisión Nacional para el Conocimiento y Uso de la Biodiversidad|CONABIO]] |access-date=2025-08-26 }}</ref><ref name="ABM">{{cite journal |last1=Cano Santana |first1=Zenón |last2=Oyama |first2=Ken |year=1994 |title=WIGANDIA URENS (HYDROPHYLLACEAE): UN MOSAICO DE RECURSOSPARA SUS INSECTOS HERBIVOROS |url=https://abm.ojs.inecol.mx/index.php/abm/article/view/715/881 |trans-title=WIGANDIA URENS (HYDROPHYLLACEAE): A MOSAIC OF RESOURCES FOR ITS HERBIVOROUS INSECTS |journal=Acta  Botánica  Mexicana  |trans-journal=Mexican Botanic Act |language=Spanish |volume=28 |publication-place=Pátzcuaro, Mexico |publisher=Instituto de Ecología A.C. |pages=29–39 |access-date=2025-08-26 }}</ref>

There are a variety of associated herbivorous insects, including [[Sphenarium purpurascens|milpa grasshopper]], [[Ichthyotettix mexicanus|conspicuous cricket]], [[Oecanthus|tree crickets]], [[Myzus persicae|green peach aphid]], [[Lintneria lugens|Chichicastlera moth]], and [[Megalographa biloba|white-spotted owl moth]], among others.<ref name="ABM" />

== Distribution and habitat ==
''Wigandia urens'' is [[Native species|native]] from Mexico south through Central America and northern South America to Trinidad and Peru. In particular it is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, much of Mexico, Nicaragua, Panamá, Peru, Trinidad-Tobago, and Venezuela.<ref name=POWO_114242-3/> In Mexico, it is distributed in Sinaloa, Durango, Nayarit, Zacatecas, Jalisco, Colima, Aguascalientes, Guanajuato, San Luis Potosí, Michoacán, Querétaro, Hidalgo, State of Mexico, Mexico City, Tlaxcala, Morelos, Guerrero, Puebla, Veracruz, Oaxaca, and Chiapas. In its native habitat, it can be found in pine-oak forests, cloud forests, low deciduous forest and xerophilous scrubland at altitudes from 20 to 3000 m above sea level.<ref name="nash" /><ref name="conabio" />

It has become naturalized in California, the Canary Islands, France, Italy, Madeira, and Spain.<ref name=POWO_114242-3/> Specimens have been found in Australia and Africa, and it is also considered an invasive species in the western Himalayas like [[Uttarakhand|Uttarakhand state]] in [[India]].<ref name="nash" /><ref name="conabio" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chandra |first1=Naveen |last2=Kumar |first2=Amit |last3=Mishra |first3=Arun Pratap |last4=Singh |first4=Gajendra |last5=Rawat |first5=Gopal Singh |year=2023 |title=Wigandia urens (Ruiz & Pav.) Kunth: a new emergent invasive alien species in the Western Himalaya |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00207233.2023.2194157 |journal=International Journal of Environmental Studies |volume=80 |issue=5 |publication-place= |publisher= |pages=1259–1272 |access-date=2025-08-26 }}</ref>

== Uses ==
It is often used for ornamental purposes, as well as ceremonial and religious purposes. It is also used as a folk remedy to treat syphilis, rheumatism, and insomnia.<ref name="flora" /><ref name="conabio" />

It is commonly grown in gardens, often under the synonym ''Wigandia caracasana''. It thrives best in a mixture of loam and peat. Cuttings in sand will strike if placed under glass and in heat.<ref>{{cite book | author=Pink, A. | url=https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11892|title=Gardening for the Million| year=2004 | publisher=[[Project Gutenberg|Project Gutenberg Literary Archive Foundation]]}}</ref>

== Dermatitis ==
It can cause severe [[contact dermatitis]].<ref>{{cite journal | pmc = 1657835 | pmid=18741724 | volume=34 | journal=Cal West Med | pages=278–9 | last1 = Anderson | first1 = NP | last2 = Ayres | first2 = S| title=Dermatitis Venenata Due to Wigandia Caracasana: A Hitherto Unrecognized Cause: Report of Case | year=1931 | issue=4 }}</ref>  A substance that it secretes, 2,3-dimethoxy-geranyl- 1,4-[[benzoquinone]] (consisting of a quinonoid ring with a 10 or 11 carbon-membered side chain), is a remarkably strong sensitizer, which is found nowhere else in the plant kingdom. It has been described as approximating an "ideal allergen".<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Hausen | first1 = B. M. | last2 = Heitsch | first2 = H. | last3 = Borrmann | first3 = B. | last4 = Koch | first4 = D. | last5 = Rathmann | first5 = R. | last6 = Richter | first6 = B. | last7 = Konig | first7 = W. A. | year = 1995 | title = Structure-activity-relationships in allergic contact-dermatitis: 1. Studies on the influence of side-chain length with derivatives of primin | journal = Contact Dermatitis | volume = 33 | pages = 12–16 | doi=10.1111/j.1600-0536.1995.tb00440.x| pmid = 7493455 | s2cid = 9025219 }}</ref>
